nodes.characterization_summary: Nano-sized CoOx is identified as primarily spinel Co3O4 with a minor rocksalt CoO phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Nano-sized CoOx is composed primarily of spinel Co3O4 with a minor rocksalt CoO component (Supplementary Figs. 1 and 2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ hard X-ray absorption spectroscopy determines the bulk average Co oxidation state of the nano CoOx to be approximately 2.52+.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The bulk averaged Co oxidation state of nano CoOx is around 2.52+ , close to 2.67+ for the Co3O4 reference (Supplementary Fig. 3).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS spectra confirm the spinel structure with a characteristic Co–O scattering contribution at approximately 1.91 Å.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The corresponding Fourier-transformed extended X-ray absorption fine-structure (EXAFS) spectrum of nano-sized CoOx shows three representative scattering contributions of the spinel structure, with a Co–O of ~1.91 Å

nodes.characterization_summary: Surface-sensitive soft X-ray absorption (sXAS) at the Co L-edge reveals a coexistence of low-spin CoIII and CoII species with a branching ratio of 0.58.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Surface-sensitive Co L3 spectra show the coexistence of CoIII species and CoII species... the branching ratios of Co L3 and Co L2 edges were calculated to be 0.58 (Supplementary Table 2), suggesting that Co is in the low-spin state

nodes.characterization_summary: Cyclic voltammetry identifies pH-dependent Co(II/III) and Co(III/IV) redox transitions; alkaline conditions exhibit a higher abundance of redox-active sites compared to neutral or acidic environments.
nodes.evidence_snippet: CV curves showing the CoII/III (Vpa1 and Vpc1) and CoIII/IV (Vpa2 and Vpc2) redox features in different electrolytes... indicates the redox-active Co site is more abundant in the alkaline electrolyte
